item_title: Two student researchers graduate after a season in the field
item_introduction: Aaliyah Thompson completes her undergraduate thesis on sensor drift, and Grace Kim finishes her project on field-kit instrument housings.

add_image.image_alt: A researcher preparing sampling equipment at a bench
add_image.image_caption: Bench checks before the morning field shift.

add_paragraph: The lab marked the end of the field season with two graduations. **Aaliyah Thompson** submitted her undergraduate thesis on low-cost sensor calibration and drift monitoring, work that now underpins the dense particulate network the group runs across three sites.

**Grace Kim** completed her final-year project on field-kit design: sensor housings, labelling systems and the student-friendly assembly instructions that go out with every outreach kit. Her housings are already in use on the coastal campaign.

Both students joined as part of the lab's training programme, which pairs every new researcher with a bench mentor and a field mentor. Aaliyah continues with us as an MSc student; Grace starts an engineering degree in the spring.
The lab keeps a copy of both reports in the internal archive, and the kit drawings are released alongside the open-science sensor dataset.
